name: Vouvray

rules.yield_base: 52 hl/ha for still white, 65 for sparkling

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
keyfacts: Sec Vouvray may hold up to 8 g/L of residual sugar, moelleux wines up to 45 g/L, and doux wines 45 g/L or more.
The plateau rests on soft tuffeau chalk, with clay-limestone soils on the slopes and clay-siliceous soils at the plateau edges, and cellars were dug into the tuffeau.
Sparkling Vouvray is made by the traditional method and can be pétillant (semi-sparkling) or mousseux (fully sparkling).

notes: Vouvray is Chenin Blanc, made from dry (sec) through off-dry (demi-sec) to sweet (moelleux and doux), and sparkling.
Cool years favor dry and sparkling wines, while warm years bring sweet and even botrytized wines.
Depending on style, it shows honey, nuts, ginger, fig, apple and white flowers.
Traditional high-acid examples can need three to seven years in bottle before the acidity softens.

blurb.text: A Loire Valley wine area just east of Tours, in Touraine, devoted almost entirely to Chenin Blanc. Style follows the weather: cooler years favor dry and sparkling Vouvray, warmer years the sweet moelleux and liquoreux styles.
